text:
mike: Heads up — on canary I see a ~400ms main-thread stall when toggling filters on the metrics chart. Replay attached: https://s3.redwood/trace/1748502468

jana: repro for me too in EU canary, only when multiple series are visible (:four: or more).

rachel: weird — flamegraph looks like sourcemap parsing + chart-renderer module init. large chunk xfer ~1.3MB then parse spike.

mike: stack: parseSourcemap -> decodeSource -> applyLocaleStrings. telemetry import shows eager init of tel-client in that path.

jana: tl;dr: we bundle tel-client and heavy formatter into the same split used by the chart. when filter toggles we rehydrate that split.

tim: is this a k-v cache miss thing or pure parse/compile? metrics show kvcache misses but main blocker is parse on first interaction.

rachel: both. routing change last week caused different bundle affinity so more clients fetch that split on first interaction (kvcache affinity drift).

mike: quick triage plan: 1) revert routing weight tweak for charts 2) lazy-load tel-client behind a feature flag 3) split out formatter heavy code into a new async chunk. canary PR incoming.

jana: +1. also propose a small server-side API that returns pre-aggregated ticks for the filter window — makes client cheaper. that's product/infra work though.

tim: debate: adding server pre-agg reduces client CPU but increases backend QPS and complexity. might be a good ops win for large dashboards.

rachel: short-term I'd prefer client chunk split + telemetry lazy-init. long-term we can instrument an /agg route and rate-limit it behind console tier.

ops-bot: deploy started for mike/console/chart-split-lazy  — canary to 10% — ETA 15m.

mike: will add telemetry probe to measure first-interaction main-thread time and bundle fetch size before/after.

jana: also adding a quick Canary UX check: toggle filter 10x, record LCP/interaction-to-paint.

tim: if revert routing weights is needed, we should coordinate with infra — that affects prefetch affinity. I'm opening infra ticket.

rachel: FYI logging: I saw 2 clients in EU repeatedly re-fetching same split because CDN cache-control headers dropped s-maxage after the routing change. that explains repeated parse hits.

jana: great catch. that plus sourcemap parse is the multiplier. we should patch CDN header + split.

mike: ok action items: mike PR (split + lazy tel-client) -> canary 10% (ops-bot) -> infra ticket for routing revert + CDN header fix -> jana to prototype /agg idea. I'll post updates here.

ops-bot: canary finished (10%). metrics: first-interaction main-thread down 45% in canary vs baseline, bundle fetch size reduced by 820KB on average.

jana: awesome. rolling the split to 50% after infra confirms CDN header fix.

tim: ping infra, ticket #INF-4821: revert routing weight  (blocks 50% rollout).

mike: thanks everyone. follow-ups: I'll open an RFC for the /agg API so we can weigh cost/benefit before product asks.

rachel: filing a tiny postmortem note for the rollout doc — improbable interaction between routing affinity + CDN headers + eager telemetry import.

mike: closing loop once 50% looks stable. :thumbsup:
